drop.title: The Game You Are Guaranteed to Win and Cannot Learn to

title: The Game You Are Guaranteed
to Win, and Cannot Learn to
slides.dek: Chomp is a two-player game with a one-line proof that the first player always wins. The proof produces no move, no rule, no plan. It is the cleanest example of knowing a thing exists without knowing what it is.

slides.body: A rectangle of cookies. On your turn you eat one, and every cookie above it and to its right vanishes too. The bottom-left cookie is poisoned; whoever is forced to eat it loses. That is the whole game, and the first player can *always* win it, on every board bigger than one cookie. The proof is one paragraph. Suppose instead the *second* player had a guaranteed winning reply to the tiny top-right bite. Then the first player could have just opened with that reply and stolen it. The assumption eats itself, so the first player wins. It has a name: *strategy-stealing.*

Read that proof again and look for the winning move. It is not there. It proves a winner *exists* by showing the opposite is self-contradictory, and hands you a guarantee wrapped around an empty box. On the 3×4 board there is *exactly one* winning first move, and the proof will not say which cookie. Only searching every branch will. For a few shapes we can fill the box: on a *square*, eat the second cookie down the diagonal, then mirror your opponent forever. Two-row boards have a one-line rule. Add a third row and the losing set turns *jagged*, with no formula anyone has ever found.

lines.sub: rotate format back to game (three of the last four were research #041/#039/#037; last game #038, three drops back). picked chomp (gale, 1974): the game with a one-line proof the first player wins that names no move. sits by nim/wythoff but breaks both spines, no XOR, no formula

three modules over one memoized solver: play a perfect machine on five boards (you move first, so a win exists); strategy-stealing drawn as three panels; the square mirror + 2xn staircase beside the jagged 3-row losing set that has no formula

checked offline first: first player wins every board but 1x1 for all m,n to 8, 0 wrong of 64; eat(1,1) is the unique winning opening on squares n=2..6; the 2xn losers are exactly the bottom-row-one-longer shapes; the 3xn losing set stays jagged, 29 positions to width 10; exactly one winning first move on each preset board

slides.sub: Play Chomp against a machine that never errs, on five boards where a winning line is guaranteed to exist, and try to find the one first move the proof refuses to name. See strategy-stealing drawn in three panels, the square mirror trick, the two-row staircase, and beside them the three-row losing set that stays jagged with no formula. Wythoff's game hid a golden-ratio rule under the surface; Chomp proves the rule is there and never lets you see it.
